title: No, None and Negative Pronouns
summary: Express zero quantity or complete absence using no + noun, none alone or none of a defined group, and nothing, nobody or nowhere. Rewrite these meanings with not ... any without using double negatives in standard English, and distinguish negative absence from any meaning unrestricted possibility.
learningObjectives: Use no before a noun, none without a following noun, and none of with a defined group or quantity.
Express absence using nothing, nobody/no one and nowhere in subjects, objects and short answers.
Rewrite negative-pronoun sentences using not ... any without adding a second negative in standard English.
Use appropriate subject agreement and gender-neutral reference with none of and nobody; distinguish negative no from free-choice any.

explanation.heading: No + noun; none without a following noun
explanation.body: Use no directly before a noun to say zero members or zero amount: no spare cables, no information, no opportunity. No itself makes the clause negative; do not add not simply to repeat this meaning. Use none when the noun is understood from context: Asked how many copies remain, you can answer None. Do not follow none directly with a noun: none copies is incorrect. In a negative clause, not ... any often communicates the same absence.
explanation.example: The event has no remaining places, and the later session has none either.

explanation.heading: None of: zero from a specific group
explanation.body: Use none of when referring to a defined set: none of the proposals, none of these, none of us. After none of + plural noun or pronoun, both singular and plural verb agreement can be possible, although plural agreement is common in everyday speech. With an uncountable noun, singular agreement is usual: none of the equipment is ready. Do not confuse none of the students with no students: both may describe zero, but none of explicitly identifies a group.
explanation.example: None of the three speakers were available for the rescheduled meeting.

explanation.heading: Nothing, nobody/no one and nowhere
explanation.body: These pronouns and adverbs express complete absence: nothing for things, nobody or no one for people, and nowhere for places. They can be subjects, objects or stand-alone answers. They already have negative meaning, so standard English does not combine them with an additional negative verb to mean zero. You can use them after be or have: there is nothing missing; the team has nowhere to store the crates.
explanation.example: No one answered the intercom when the courier arrived.

explanation.heading: Two equivalent ways to express a negative
explanation.body: Compare a negative pronoun with a positive verb and an any-word after a negative verb: I heard nothing / I did not hear anything. For people, The organiser told nobody can be restated as The organiser did not tell anybody; the meaning stays negative without combining not with nobody. However, I didn't hear nothing is nonstandard if you intend to say you heard nothing. Some dialects use negative concord; the exercises here practise standard written English. When you rewrite, preserve the intended meaning.
explanation.example: The visitor told nobody about the delay, so nobody was prepared.

explanation.heading: Singular pronouns, singular they and any as free choice
explanation.body: Nobody and no one are singular subjects: nobody knows, no one was. They, them and their can naturally refer back to these words without specifying gender: Nobody brought their badge. By contrast, any or anybody can express unrestricted choice or possibility, not absence: Anyone may submit a proposal. Compare no seat is available with any seat is acceptable: the first excludes all seats, while the second includes every choice.
explanation.example: Nobody on the shortlist has changed their contact details.

left.label: No before a noun
left.example: The shelter has no blankets left.
left.note: No is a determiner followed directly by the noun blankets.

right.label: None without the noun
right.example: The shelter used its final blankets; none are left.
right.note: None stands alone because blankets is understood.

left.label: Negative pronoun
left.note: Nobody already expresses that zero people noticed.

right.label: Negative verb plus any-word
right.example: The team did not tell anybody about the incorrect date.
right.note: Did not ... anybody expresses absence using the negative verb, with no negative-concord doubling.

left.label: No means zero
left.example: No seats in the front row are available.
left.note: The front row cannot be used.

right.label: Any means unrestricted selection
right.example: You can take any seat in the back row.
right.note: Every back-row seat is an acceptable option.

examples.sentence: We found no evidence of damage during the inspection.
examples.note: No directly determines the uncountable noun evidence.

examples.sentence: Four applicants were shortlisted, but none accepted the offer.
examples.note: None means none of the four applicants, so the noun need not be repeated.

examples.sentence: None of the documents are signed yet.
examples.note: None of introduces a specific plural group; plural agreement is natural.

examples.sentence: The room was silent; nobody spoke during the announcement.
examples.note: Nobody as a subject means no person spoke and takes a singular verb.

examples.sentence: The supplier has nowhere to park the delivery van.
examples.note: Nowhere indicates that no suitable place exists.

examples.sentence: We didn't find anything useful in the archive.
examples.note: Not ... anything is equivalent here to found nothing.

examples.sentence: No one left their phone number at reception.
examples.note: No one is singular, while their gives a natural gender-neutral reference.

commonMistakes.incorrect: None reports were submitted before the deadline.
commonMistakes.correct: No reports were submitted before the deadline.
commonMistakes.why: No, not none, goes directly before a noun.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We found nothing useful and did not see nobody.
commonMistakes.correct: We found nothing useful and did not see anybody.
commonMistakes.why: In standard English, combine a negative verb with anybody, not nobody, to mean zero people seen.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Nobody know when the meeting starts.
commonMistakes.correct: Nobody knows when the meeting starts.
commonMistakes.why: Nobody is grammatically singular and requires knows in the present simple.

commonMistakes.incorrect: There is not nowhere to charge the laptop.
commonMistakes.correct: There is nowhere to charge the laptop.
commonMistakes.why: Nowhere already expresses absence; remove not in a standard negative statement.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I have no of the receipts.
commonMistakes.correct: I have none of the receipts.
commonMistakes.why: Before of + a specific group, use none of rather than no of.

studyTips: Before a noun, choose no; without a repeated noun, choose none; before of + a defined set, choose none of.
Rewrite three pairs aloud: Nobody answered / No one answered / I did not hear from anybody; Nothing changed / We did not change anything.
For sentences with a negative verb, scan for nobody, nothing and nowhere; replace them with an any-word when the intended meaning is zero.
Compare examples with no and any and ask whether the speaker means zero options or permission to pick whichever option they like.

exercises.prompt: The laboratory ran out of spare gloves. There were ___ pairs left.
exercises.feedback: No must stand before the plural noun pairs; none would replace rather than modify that noun.

exercises.prompt: Three people were invited to give a talk, but ___ agreed to come.
exercises.feedback: None replaces the understood noun people and means zero out of the invited group.

exercises.prompt: The trainee checked each of the six labels. ___ of them matched the correct code.
exercises.feedback: None of them refers to zero out of the previously identified six labels.

exercises.prompt: The door was locked, and ___ could tell us the new entry code.
exercises.feedback: Nobody expresses that no person could tell them the code without requiring an additional negative verb.

exercises.prompt: The workshop has ___ spare seats, so registration has closed. (one word before the noun)
acceptedAnswers: no
exercises.feedback: No + a plural noun expresses the absence of spare seats.

exercises.prompt: There were five replies expected, but ___ had arrived by noon. (one word replacing the noun replies)
acceptedAnswers: none
exercises.feedback: None means zero out of the expected replies and does not require a following noun.

exercises.prompt: ___ of these four computers is connected to the network. (one word before of; use singular verb already given)
acceptedAnswers: none
exercises.feedback: None of identifies zero members of the four-computer set; is is an accepted singular agreement option here.

exercises.prompt: The boxes were empty. There was ___ inside them. (one negative pronoun for things)
acceptedAnswers: nothing
exercises.feedback: Nothing means that no object was inside any of the boxes.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: None employees received the updated timetable.
acceptedAnswers: No employees received the updated timetable.
exercises.feedback: No is used directly before a noun; none cannot modify employees.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence by replacing only the final negative word: The driver did not find nowhere to unload the van.
acceptedAnswers: The driver did not find anywhere to unload the van.
exercises.feedback: Not ... anywhere expresses that no unloading place was found in standard English.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Nobody in the queue know where the entrance is.
acceptedAnswers: Nobody in the queue knows where the entrance is.
exercises.feedback: Nobody is grammatically singular, so the verb must be knows.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I have no of the documents you requested.
acceptedAnswers: I have none of the documents you requested.
exercises.feedback: Use none of before the specific documents, not no of.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make one complete sentence using these facts: the café / have / no / outdoor tables. Use the present simple.
acceptedAnswers: The café has no outdoor tables.
speakingExercises.feedback: No directly modifies the plural noun outdoor tables.

speakingExercises.prompt: A colleague asks how many spare cables remain. Exactly zero remain. Reply in one complete sentence, starting with “There” and ending with “none left”.
acceptedAnswers: There are none left.
speakingExercises.feedback: None substitutes for the understood noun spare cables; are agrees naturally with the plural items.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make one sentence using: none of / the five reports / be / ready. Use the present simple and plural agreement.
acceptedAnswers: None of the five reports are ready.
speakingExercises.feedback: None of the five reports identifies a defined plural group; are is a natural choice.

speakingExercises.prompt: A visitor asks, “Who answered the help-line call?” The fact is that no person answered. Reply in one sentence beginning “Nobody” and ending “the call”.
acceptedAnswers: Nobody answered the call.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nobody is a negative subject and does not need a negative verb.

speakingExercises.prompt: Rephrase this sentence using not ... anything, without changing its meaning: “We found nothing in the storage room.”
acceptedAnswers: We didn't find anything in the storage room.
We did not find anything in the storage room.
speakingExercises.feedback: A negative verb plus anything expresses the same absence as found nothing.

speakingExercises.prompt: Someone asks whether you found a suitable parking space. You found no suitable place. Reply in one sentence beginning “I” and ending “to park”, using nowhere.
acceptedAnswers: I found nowhere to park.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nowhere expresses that no place to park was found.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say exactly two sentences using these facts: nobody / bring / an ID badge (past simple); they / have / to return to reception (past simple). Begin the second sentence with “They”.
acceptedAnswers: Nobody brought an ID badge. They had to return to reception.
speakingExercises.feedback: Nobody is a singular negative subject; they can refer back to the people concerned.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct the double negative and say the complete sentence, changing only the negative pronoun: “I did not see nobody in the corridor.”
acceptedAnswers: I did not see anybody in the corridor.
I didn't see anybody in the corridor.
speakingExercises.feedback: After did not, anybody is the standard form meaning no person was seen.

choices: The repair has already been completed.
listeningExercises.feedback: No replacement screens means the needed parts have run out.
listeningExercises.audioText: The repair centre has no replacement screens left, so we cannot complete your repair today.

listeningExercises.prompt: How many of the proposals met the requirements?
listeningExercises.feedback: None means zero of the six proposals satisfied the requirements.
listeningExercises.audioText: Six proposals reached the committee, but none met the safety requirements for approval.

listeningExercises.prompt: Type the single negative pronoun immediately after “was”.
acceptedAnswers: nothing
listeningExercises.feedback: Nothing signals that no other contents were present beyond the stated exception.
listeningExercises.audioText: There was nothing in the parcel except a folded instruction sheet.

listeningExercises.prompt: What problem did the receptionist have?
choices: The visitors signed under the wrong dates.
There was no written record of arrivals.
The book had been taken to another office.
listeningExercises.feedback: No one signed means the required arrivals were not recorded.
listeningExercises.audioText: No one signed the visitor book, so the receptionist could not check who had arrived.

listeningExercises.prompt: What was the outcome of the search?
choices: They found a suitable room upstairs.
They cancelled the search before it started.
No suitable location was available on that floor.
listeningExercises.feedback: Nowhere suitable means the search did not produce an acceptable place.
listeningExercises.audioText: We searched the whole floor, but there was nowhere suitable to hold the extra training session.

choices: All members may borrow it, but it must stay on site overnight.
Only senior members are allowed to borrow it.
Nobody can borrow the equipment at all.
listeningExercises.feedback: Any member opens borrowing to everyone; no member forbids taking equipment home overnight.
listeningExercises.audioText: Any member can borrow the equipment, but no member may take it home overnight.

listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two words at the beginning of the recording.
acceptedAnswers: None of
listeningExercises.feedback: None of introduces a defined group from which zero vans were available.
listeningExercises.audioText: None of the four delivery vans were available when the shift began.

listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word expression heard immediately after “find”.
acceptedAnswers: anything useful
listeningExercises.feedback: Not ... anything useful describes a negative result without a second negative word.
listeningExercises.audioText: I did not find anything useful in the notes from the previous meeting.
